RheumaFinder describes RFMapple as "the world's first AI-based software platform for opportunistic rheumatism screening" — built to run as a concurrent reading aid on top of whatever PACS a hospital already has.
Organization
RheumaFinder is a Ghent, Belgium-based health-tech startup building RFMapple, an AI add-on that opportunistically screens CT scans hospitals already perform for other reasons for early signs of rheumatic disease — erosion and ankylosis in the sacroiliac joints. source ↗
Clinical / business profile
PACS-agnostic, cloud-native SaaS on a pay-per-use model; the clinical validation version reported at least 70% sensitivity and 90% specificity for detecting joint erosion and ankylosis. Backed by life-sciences investor Novalis Biotech since May 2024. source ↗
Contact
Thomas Van Den Berghe, MD, PhD — Chief Medical Officer, RheumaFinder; co-founder, and specialist in AI and musculoskeletal radiology. source ↗
Momentum
Wim Van Hecke, PhD — founder and CEO of icometrix, a leading Belgian medical-imaging AI company — joined RheumaFinder's board in March 2026, just as the company runs CrossCare 2.0 field testing with radiologists and rheumatologists across Flanders and the Netherlands en route to TRL8. source ↗
Why now: RheumaFinder is mid-rollout of CrossCare 2.0 (through March 2026), actively field-testing RFMapple with radiologists and rheumatologists at sites in Flanders (Zorglab Aalst) and the Netherlands (Zuyd Hogeschool) on the path to TRL8 — exactly the stage where every new hospital's PACS/RIS/EHR combination becomes a fresh integration project instead of a configuration.
Vorro · the whole record at the point of care — medications, labs, notes, imaging, outside encounters
The Integration Pitch

Scaling Screening Without Scaling Integrations

RheumaFinder built RFMapple to catch rheumatic disease years earlier by reading CT scans a hospital is already taking for something else — but the moment that AI finding needs to reach the ordering radiologist, the referring rheumatologist, and the patient's own record, it runs into as many data formats as there are hospitals. Every new PACS, RIS, or EHR combination the CrossCare 2.0 rollout adds across Flanders and the Netherlands is another interface to build, test, and maintain by hand.

The highest-leverage moment is now, while RheumaFinder is still early in scaling from a handful of validation sites toward what it calls "the world's first AI-based platform for opportunistic rheumatism screening." Vorro can sit underneath RFMapple as the interoperability layer that turns every new hospital onboarding from a bespoke integration project into a configuration exercise — DICOM and imaging metadata in, structured FHIR findings out, to whichever PACS, RIS, or EHR that site already runs.

That is the difference between RheumaFinder spending its engineering hours on model accuracy versus interface plumbing, and it's the difference for hospitals between a pilot that stays a pilot and opportunistic screening that becomes a standard part of every CT read. With Wim Van Hecke — who scaled icometrix's own imaging AI across hundreds of sites — now on the board, that scaling question is exactly where RheumaFinder is headed next.
